item.title: Mavericks star Cooper Flagg exits vs. Pacers after hard foul
item.description: The Dallas Mavericks announced that Cooper Flagg will not return to Friday's game against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis due to left shoulder soreness.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Dallas Mavericks announced that Cooper Flagg will not return to Friday's game against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis due to left shoulder soreness. The second-year star took a hard foul late in the second quarter and did not return to the floor to start the second half. With 59.7 seconds left in the first half, Indiana's Aaron Nesmith challenged Flagg's dunk attempt from behind, sending Flagg sprawling to the floor. After a review, Nesmith was assessed a flagrant-1 foul. Naji Marshall rushed in and shoved Nesmith, resulting in technical fouls for both players. Dallas carried a 77-43 lead into the locker room. Flagg, the reigning NBA Rookie of the Year, notched 14 points, six assists and five rebounds in 17 minutes of first-half play before being ruled out. The 19-year-old registered 32 points and five rebounds in the Mavericks' season-opening loss to the Houston Rockets. He averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.5 assists in 70 games last season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Suspect arrested as fire engulfs Nazi guest house 'Eagle's Nest', German police say

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German police said they had detained a suspect after fire broke out at a historic mountain guest house known as the "Eagle's Nest" that was a used as a retreat for Nazi officials. Around 200 fire fighters and emergency personnel in the area around Berchtesgaden in the southern region of Bavaria were battling the flames after the building, known as the Kehlsteinhaus, caught fire on Friday, police said.

item.title: Jake Evans tallies twice, adds assist as Canadiens topple Blackhawks
item.description: Jake Evans produced two goals and an assist and Jacob Fowler stopped 20 shots, lifting the visiting Montreal Canadiens to a 4-1 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jake Evans produced two goals and an assist and Jacob Fowler stopped 20 shots, lifting the visiting Montreal Canadiens to a 4-1 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Friday. Kaiden Guhle added a goal and assist to help Montreal earn its first road victory since opening night. Mike Matheson also scored as the Canadiens improved to 4-1-1 in their past six games. Connor Bedard scored and Spencer Knight made 24 saves as the Blackhawks fell to 2-3-0 on a seven-game homestand. Chicago started strong, as Bedard opened the scoring at 4:23 of the first period on a snap shot from just outside the left circle. After a Montreal dump-in glanced off a linesman, Patrick Kane collected the puck and slid it to a streaking Bedard in the neutral zone. Montreal, playing without captain and top center Nick Suzuki (upper body), struggled to find offensive footing in the early going. The Canadiens needed 3:31 to record their first shot on goal and didn't register another for another 2 1/2 minutes. Evans tallied the equalizer at 17:29 of the first period, beating Knight with a wrist shot from in front of the net off a feed from Kirby Dach. Montreal took the lead on Evans' short-handed goal at 7:45 of the second period. With the Canadiens pressuring the Blackhawks' five-forward power play, a Kane shot attempt redirected off Tyler Bertuzzi's skate and created an odd-man rush for Montreal. Evans carried the puck down the left side and scored from the circle. Fowler turned aside Roman Kantserov and Kane on a Chicago rush moments later to preserve a one-goal advantage. The Canadiens made it 3-1 at 18:26 of the second. Guhle netted his first goal of the season on a wrist shot from the point. Chicago finished 0-for-5 on the power play compared to 0-for-3 for Montreal. The Blackhawks' final man advantage of the game lasted just 22 seconds in the third period, as Teuvo Teravainen was whistled for interference moments after Montreal's Juraj Slafkovsky was penalized for hooking. Matheson's empty-net goal at 17:22 accounted for the final margin. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kraken aim to stay hot against road-weary Wild
item.description: The Seattle Kraken will try to extend their winning streak to three games Saturday when they host the Minnesota Wild, who have lost the first two games of a five-game road trip.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Seattle Kraken will try to extend their winning streak to three games Saturday when they host the Minnesota Wild, who have lost the first two games of a five-game road trip. Minnesota fell 4-3 in a shootout Tuesday at Edmonton and 2-1 Thursday at Calgary, dropping to 0-1-1 on its road trip. The Wild visit Vancouver on Sunday and Utah on Tuesday to complete the trip. "That's two games in a row we lost the special teams battle and it cost us," said Wild forward Blake Coleman, who was in the penalty box for Calgary's first goal. "You've got guys sitting on the bench that need to be on the ice. Three penalties in a row in the first period is not the recipe and I'm certainly part of that. I'll clean it up. I know we all will and we'll go from there." Michael McCarron scored the lone goal for Minnesota in the third period and goalie Jesper Wallstedt made 20 saves. "We battled back and gave ourselves a chance, but ultimately, it wasn't good enough," Minnesota coach John Hynes said. Kirill Kaprizov, the Wild's leading scorer with 17 points in 11 games (11 goals, six assists), saw his seven-game point streak (eight goals, six assists) and four-game goal streak snapped. Minnesota defensemen Jared Spurgeon and Olli Maatta returned Thursday after missing four and three games, respectively, with upper-body injuries. Forward Maxim Shabanov (upper body) was a late scratch and Hynes said he's day-to-day. "If you give up two goals and you're trying to chase the whole game, it's tough playing that way," Maatta said. "Kudos to them for defending hard, but also I think we got our chances and that just showed the way we've got to play the full 60." The Wild will face a surging Seattle squad that's 5-1-1 over its past seven games, including a 5-3 win over Utah on Thursday, with Mackie Samoskevich scoring the tiebreaking goal at 14:35 of the third period and goaltender Philipp Grubauer making 33 saves. Jordan Eberle and Brandon Montour had a goal and an assist apiece and Matty Beniers and Frederick Gaudreau also tallied for the Kraken, who are 2-0-0 on their four-game homestand that wraps up next Wednesday against Toronto. It was the second straight game Seattle overcame a blown multi-goal third-period lead. The Kraken surrendered a 3-1 advantage against Utah after allowing Detroit to erase a 3-0 deficit Tuesday before winning 4-3 in a shootout. "If you want to look at it from a positive standpoint, we're getting into a position where we're able to give up a multi-goal lead and still win," Kraken coach Lane Lambert said. "We've got to continue to play the game the same way that got us the lead, and that comes with a little bit of experience, a little bit of time. What it says about our team's resilience in these situations, it says a lot." Beniers wasn't as sympathetic. "We got to learn from it," the forward said. "We have to get better playing with leads and shutting teams down and not letting them push back." --Field Level Media

item.title: Pistons jump out to big lead, hand Heat second straight loss
item.description: John Collins scored 23 points and grabbed seven rebounds, and Paul Reed finished with 19 points and 11 rebounds to lead the Detroit Pistons to a 128-111 victory over the host Miami Heat on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: John Collins scored 23 points and grabbed seven rebounds, and Paul Reed finished with 19 points and 11 rebounds to lead the Detroit Pistons to a 128-111 victory over the host Miami Heat on Friday night. The Pistons (2-0) led wire to wire after scoring the game's first 11 points and built a lead of as many as 23 in the third quarter. The Heat (0-2) never got closer than eight points after Detroit's early surge despite another strong outing from Giannis Antetokounmpo. Antetokounmpo scored a game-high 36 points, grabbed 12 rebounds and dished out five assists for his first double-double in a Miami uniform. Collins, who shot 5-of-6 from 3-point range, helped Detroit build a 22-5 lead and spearheaded a 47.4% effort from beyond the arc (18-of-38). The Pistons shot 52.8% from the field (47-of-89), with former Heat guard Duncan Robinson making five of 10 3-point attempts and finishing with 17 points. It was another subpar defensive effort for Miami, which allowed 21 3-pointers and 131 points in its season-opening loss to Minnesota on Wednesday. The Heat were hampered in the first half when Bam Adebayo picked up three fouls in the first quarter and sat with 1:13 remaining. Adebayo did not return until the start of the second half. He finished with just four points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals before fouling out. Detroit's Cade Cunningham committed seven turnovers but finished with 16 points and eight assists. Daniss Jenkins scored 15 points, while Isaiah Joe chipped in 12. Miami made 15 3-pointers but shot just 29.4% from long range on 51 attempts. Davion Mitchell totaled 18 points and five rebounds, while Bobby Portis Jr. had 11 points and eight rebounds. The Heat shot just 38.2% from the field. Pistons center Jalen Duren left with 6:45 remaining in the second quarter due to a right thigh injury and did not return. He finished with four points and six rebounds in 10 minutes. --Field Level Media

item.title: US accuses government contractor of leaking classified info to girlfriend's Substack
item.description: The US Justice Department accused a government contractor on Friday of leaking national defense information to his girlfriend, the publisher of a Substack newsletter.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Trotta
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department accused a government contractor on Friday of leaking national defense information to his girlfriend, the publisher of a Substack newsletter. The FBI arrested Ian Brinksman, 42, on Friday following a search of his Washington home, a Justice Department statement said. Prosecutors charged him with unlawfully transmitting national defense information. A federal public defender representing Brinksman declined to comment. “As alleged, Brinksman reached far outside his own duties to obtain some of our Nation’s most closely held secrets and handed them to a romantic partner he knew intended to publish them,” John Eisenberg, assistant attorney general for national security, said in the statement. “That is not carelessness. It is a betrayal of his oath and the American people who entrusted him to fulfill his duties honorably,” Eisenberg said. Brinksman held a top secret security clearance while working as an employee of a US government agency and later as a developer for systems integration for a private contractor working for the same agency, prosecutors said. According to the sworn affidavit of an FBI agent investigating the case, Brinksman repeatedly accessed classified intelligence reports and then communicated with the journalist. The affidavit also cites phone records, database access logs, badge-swipe records, emails and other evidence. The affidavit only identifies the journalist as "Individual 1," but it cites excerpts from articles she published. "A fundraising article reportedly published by Individual 1 in September 2026 stated 'over the past year [Individual 1 has] published reporting based on classified [relevant U.S. government agency] assessments that I believe the public deserves to know about,'" the affidavit reads. That quote appears in a September 28 piece published on the Capital & Empire online newsletter authored by Aída Chávez. "Over the past year, I’ve published reporting based on classified CIA assessments that I believe the public deserves to know about," wrote Chávez, whose profile on the site notes that she worked for The Nation and other outlets before she launched the newsletter. Chávez did not immediately respond to an email message seeking comment. Investigators allege that on at least five occasions in 2026, Individual 1 published Substack articles containing information that mirrored the classified reports, some at the top secret level. On some of those dates, Chávez published articles that cite classified reports, some of them attributed to the CIA. According to a LinkedIn profile bearing Brinksman's name, he worked for Deloitte as a manager and as a senior strategy security consultant after having worked as a US State Department foreign service officer at dates corresponding to those outlined in the Justice Department statement. Deloitte did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The State Department said it needed more time to respond before commenting.

item.title: Red Wings look to extend dominance over Flames
item.description: Two teams battling to stay in the win column square off in Calgary as the Flames host the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Two teams battling to stay in the win column square off in Calgary as the Flames host the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday. This is the first of two meetings between these teams this season. Detroit has won eight straight in the overall series dating back to the 2022-23 season. The Red Wings appear to have righted the ship after a lackluster start, winning three of their last four games. They played a consistent game to win 2-1 against the lowly Philadelphia Flyers, rallied late for a 4-3 shootout victory against the San Jose Sharks, and most recently secured an early lead in a 5-2 win against the Vancouver Canucks. On Thursday in Vancouver, Lucas Raymond scored twice in the first period to give Detroit a 3-1 lead. "He put himself in good spots tonight to score," Red Wings head coach Todd McLellan said. "I thought he did that last game. Even when he mishandled the puck a couple times three or four games ago, he was in the right spot. So now he's feeling good, the confidence is back where it should be, and hopefully he takes off." William Wallinder and Michael Rasmussen also scored. John Gibson stopped four of five shots over two periods but did not return for the third due to an apparent eye issue, according to McLellan. Michal Postava, recalled from the AHL earlier that day, made seven saves in his NHL debut. "It's crazy," Postava said. "I think it's for me the best option. I don't have time to think about anything, so yeah, I just warm up and be ready." The Flames have also won three of their last four, after starting their 2026-27 campaign with five straight losses. They rallied in the third period to secure a 4-2 win over the Anaheim Ducks, scored a third-period goal to top the defending champion Carolina Hurricanes 3-2, and leaned on Devin Cooley to lock down a 2-1 win over the Minnesota Wild. Cooley made 34 saves against the Hurricanes and 36 against the Wild. "The last five or 10 minutes, I was like, 'Okay, now it's my turn. Like to return the favor a little bit,'" Cooley said following the win against Minnesota. "The guys battled so hard for me. I wanted to battle for them." Aydar Suniev and Joel Farabee scored first-period power-play goals, giving the Flames an early 2-0 lead. Minnesota outshot Calgary 17-3 in the third period in an effort to rally and tie the game late, which is where Flames head coach Ryan Huska said Cooley really stood tall. "For two periods, I thought we were really good," Huska recalled. "I thought we did a lot of good things against a good team. In the third period, our goaltender was our best player. When you find yourself in situations when you're really pushing for a win, sometimes you take on a little water, and when we did, he was unreal." --Field Level Media

item.title: Golden Knights, Blue Jackets bothered after blowout losses
item.description: The Vegas Golden Knights bring a streak of four straight 6-2 games into their Saturday road contest against the Columbus Blue Jackets.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Vegas Golden Knights bring a streak of four straight 6-2 games into their Saturday road contest against the Columbus Blue Jackets. The good news for the Golden Knights? They won the first two games in that span, defeating the Calgary Flames and the Pittsburgh Penguins. The bad news? They carry a two-game losing streak into Ohio, which includes a setback against the St. Louis Blues on Thursday in the opener of their two-game road trip. The Golden Knights, who advanced to the Stanley Cup Final last season behind strong defense and solid goaltending, allowed only 24 goals over their first 10 games of the season, so allowing 12 goals in their back-to-back losses to the Tampa Bay Lightning and St. Louis could be considered concerning. "A little bit," said Vegas center Jack Eichel, who leads the team with 19 points and 13 assists. "I feel like it's just sloppy play on our own part. The last two hasn't been like us. I think it's a good opportunity for us all to look in the mirror and know we have to be better as a group, all five guys on the ice at a time, working with our goaltender. "I don't want to say concerning because obviously we know we have it in this room, but you don't want to give up that many goals in back-to-back games. ... We as a team have to be better." Before the recent slump, Vegas had allowed a total of six goals in its three previous games, and just four goals in a contest twice. "You don't want to give up six in back-to-back games," said veteran Golden Knights defenseman Brayden McNabb. "We'll look at it and get better. A humbling last couple of games, so we'll get better." Next up is a Columbus team coming off a 6-2 loss of its own on Tuesday against the visiting Toronto Maple Leafs. The Blue Jackets, who have garnered just six points over their first eight games, trailed 5-1 after two periods and lost despite finishing with a 38-22 edge in shots on goal. Columbus brings a two-game losing streak into the Saturday contest and has gone 1-4-0 over its past five games, including a 1-0 overtime win over the New York Rangers on Oct. 17. Only Vancouver (five) has fewer points in the league. Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness blames needless penalties combined with turnovers for his team's recent struggles. Columbus also brings in a streak of going 0-for-20 on the power play. The Blue Jackets have not scored with the man advantage since their opener against Buffalo on Oct. 1. Bowness called out his team for its sloppy play after the Tuesday defeat to the Maple Leafs. "You go back to the Rangers game, we didn't turn the puck over," Bowness said. "Then the first (period), look at all the turnovers. If it continues, people are going to start losing ice time. I'm going to have to bench some guys. If they keep taking penalties, I'm going to have to bench them. That's bringing that on themselves. "I'm out of patience with it. You want to keep saying 'I can make that play' and then not make it, and we end up playing a three-quarters ice game, then expect to lose some ice time." --Field Level Media

item.title: Typhoon Champi sweeps past Taiwan, leaving 1 dead, 500 injured
item.description: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing 1 person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continued to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there.
item.dc:creator: Yimou Lee, Angie Teo, Ann Wang
item.content:encoded: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing 1 person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continued to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there. At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi is weakening though still packing gusts of around 126 kph (78 mph) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration. The storm was about 170 km (106 miles) northeast of Taiwan, having glanced off the island's northeastern coast in Yilan County early on Saturday, the CWA said. The centre of the storm turned south around midnight, hugging the Yilan coastline before making a rare loop offshore and moving away northward. Wind gusts touched 227 kph (141 mph) in some coastal areas, knocking down power lines and sending roof tiles flying. 'MOST TERRIFYING AROUND MIDNIGHT' "It was most terrifying around midnight," said a retired teacher surnamed Lin as he inspected downed banana trees in his garden in Yilan. "It was a sleepless night. I haven't seen anything like this in many years." The storm's forecast track shows it turning north, tracking up the Chinese coast and eventually moving into southern Japan. Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remained at 1, a man swept away by waves from the island of Liuqiu, with 527 injuries during the heavy wind and torrential rain. Taipower said more than 288,000 homes had lost electricity, though most had been reconnected. The transport ministry said 259 flights were cancelled, an improvement from Friday, when the number was almost 1,000. In the capital Taipei, there were downed trees and on-off squally rain showers. Taipei resident Thomas Wang, 70, said the storm felt like something out of the horror film "Poltergeist". "It was quite scary," he said, out running morning errands. Governments in a swathe of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Saturday. Although more common in summer, typhoons can strike in autumn too. China's emergency management ministry sent a team to the eastern province of Zhejiang as Champi approached, warning of strong winds and heavy rain through Sunday. It said it had readied 400 rescue workers and 600 pieces of equipment, while more than 41,000 firefighters were on emergency duty. In Taizhou, a city on Zhejiang's coast, more than 3,800 fishing boats returned to harbour, offshore fish-farm workers were brought ashore and 2,084 island visitors were evacuated, state media reported. Authorities halted 25 offshore construction projects and suspended 18 passenger ferry routes.

item.title: Jayson Tatum puts up 36 as Celtics send Knicks to second straight loss
item.description: Jayson Tatum scored a game-high 36 points, including nine late in the fourth quarter, as the Boston Celtics withstood a late comeback bid by the visiting New York Knicks to escape with a 107-103 victory on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jayson Tatum scored a game-high 36 points, including nine late in the fourth quarter, as the Boston Celtics withstood a late comeback bid by the visiting New York Knicks to escape with a 107-103 victory on Friday. Tatum finished with nine rebounds and seven assists for the Celtics, who have split their first two games. Paul George and reserve Neemias Queta had 15 points apiece while Derrick White added 12 points. Celtics center Mitchell Robinson, the lone member of the Knicks' rotation who didn't return to the defending NBA champions, had four points and four rebounds in 22-plus minutes. Karl-Anthony Towns (22 points, 10 rebounds), OG Anunoby (20 points, 10 rebounds) and Josh Hart (10 points, 12 rebounds) all had double-doubles for the Knicks, who have lost their first two games. New York has taken consecutive losses for the first time since dropping Games 2 and 3 of an Eastern Conference first-round playoff series against the Atlanta Hawks in April, after which the Knicks won 15 of the next 16 games to clinch their first title since 1973. Miles McBride scored 20 points off the New York bench, while Jalen Brunson had 19 points. The Celtics led by as many as 12 points three times in the fourth quarter, the last at 94-82 on a three-point play by Queta, before the Knicks mounted a 9-0 run. Boston missed seven consecutive shots as New York rallied. Towns dunked to pull the Knicks within 94-91 with 4:09 left, but he missed a long 3-point attempt 28 seconds later and Tatum responded with a layup to end the Celtics' drought. The Knicks got within 99-98 on Brunson's fallaway jumper with 1:41 remaining, but Tatum sank a turnaround over Hart following a timeout and Towns was whistled for an illegal screen on the next possession. Tatum then hit a long corner fallaway, again over Hart, to extend the lead to 103-98. Anunoby answered with two free throws, but Tatum hit a 3-pointer on the next possession. McBride sank a 3-pointer before Payton Pritchard iced the win by splitting a pair of free throws with 11 seconds left. --Field Level Media

item.title: Mavericks beat Pacers as Cooper Flagg leaves with shoulder soreness
item.description: Kyrie Irving scored a game-high 24 points as the Dallas Mavericks defeated the Indiana Pacers 121-105 on Friday in Indianapolis, but the victory was overshadowed by a left shoulder injury to Cooper Flagg.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyrie Irving scored a game-high 24 points as the Dallas Mavericks defeated the Indiana Pacers 121-105 on Friday in Indianapolis, but the victory was overshadowed by a left shoulder injury to Cooper Flagg. With 59.7 seconds left in the second quarter, Aaron Nesmith challenged Flagg's dunk attempt from behind, sending him sprawling. After a review, Nesmith was assessed a flagrant-1 foul. Naji Marshall rushed in and shoved Nesmith, and both players were assessed technical fouls. Dallas carried a 77-43 lead into the locker room, but Flagg, who had 14 points, five rebounds and six assists, did not return for the second half due to left shoulder soreness. P.J. Washington added 20 points and 13 rebounds for Dallas, while Max Christie scored 16, Naji Marshall had 15 and Zaccharie Risacher contributed 11 points. Pascal Siakam paced Indiana with 23 points and Tyrese Haliburton, who missed all of last season after tearing his right Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, added 18 points in his first home game in 490 days. Andrew Nembhard scored 16 points, Obi Toppin contributed 13 points and Ivica Zubac had 11 rebounds. Dallas built a 30-17 lead on a 14-2 run, capped by Irving's layup with 3:27 left in the first quarter. Irving and Flagg hit back-to-back threes, giving Dallas a 43-25 lead as the first quarter wound down. Dallas extended its lead to 50-31 when Marshall stole the ball from Siakam and fed Risacher for a one-handed dunk with 7:55 left in the second quarter. The Mavericks eventually stretched the margin to 30 points during a 15-0 run. Toppin's three-point play capped an 8-0 Pacers run that cut their deficit to 85-62 with 4:22 left in the third quarter. Toppin's dunk cut the deficit to 106-90 with 7:38 remaining, and Haliburton's jumper trimmed it to 118-105 with 1:56 left. Dallas finished without Irving, who fouled out with 4:23 remaining. --Field Level Media

item.title: NHL-best Hurricanes close lengthy trip at energized Blues
item.description: The league-leading Carolina Hurricanes are set to close the book on a reasonably successful five-game road swing when they face the surging St. Louis Blues on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The league-leading Carolina Hurricanes are set to close the book on a reasonably successful five-game road swing when they face the surging St. Louis Blues on Saturday. Carolina took five of a possible eight points (2-1-1) during a four-game stretch against Canadian Western Conference opponents, capped off with a 6-5 shootout loss to the Edmonton Oilers on Thursday. The Hurricanes were unable to contain the Oilers' top dogs as Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl racked up two goals and three assists apiece. Juuso Valimaki handed the Hurricanes the lead with just 2:40 left in regulation. They looked poised to sneak away with the victory before McDavid sent it to the extra frame off a lucky bounce with 1:28 left. It wasn't all bad news for the defending Stanley Cup champions, though, as Seth Jarvis scored a highlight-reel goal in his first game back from offseason shoulder surgery. "The first period, I wasn't feeling too great. I was just kind of catching up to the game," Jarvis said. "After that, I thought I got my legs back and got a lot better." The 24-year-old winger went on to criticize his defensive struggles in his first game back. "One of my biggest things is defense and being responsible," he said. "I thought that part was kind of lacking (Thursday), and that's a big reason why we didn't pull this one out. Obviously, there's some stuff to clean up, but I mean, I kind of expected that coming into my first game." Sebastian Aho finished with a goal and an assist while Jordan Martinook and Shayne Gostisbehere each tallied a pair of assists. The Blues are singing a happier tune heading into the tough matchup after receiving help from an unlikely hero. Defenseman Justin Barron recorded his first career four-point game (one goal, three assists) as the Blues took down the Vegas Golden Knights 6-2 on home ice Thursday. The matchup with last season's Western Conference champions was Barron's best of the seven games he has played with St. Louis since he was claimed off waivers from the Nashville Predators on Sept. 27. "I just wanted to come in (with) obviously a little bit of a clean slate," Barron said. "Obviously, there's been some injuries here and just try to come into the lineup and prove myself." Dylan Holloway scored twice and notched an assist to extend his point streak to six games (three goals, seven assists), while Jimmy Snuggerud pitched in with a goal and an assist. Blues coach Jim Montgomery sent plenty of praise his team's way after they earned their second consecutive victory to begin a five-game homestand. "When you play this game the right way, and that was the best game we've played since the (2025 Stanley Cup) playoffs, it feels good because everybody contributed, the bench was alive," Montgomery said. "The energy on the bench was the best I've seen it in a long time and when you're doing things right, there's a saying that the hockey gods reward you." The Blues' power play has been clicking of late, scoring in each of their previous five games (6-for-17). --Field Level Media

item.title: Timberwolves cruise past Magic to sweep Florida road trip
item.description: Anthony Edwards and Jaden McDaniels scored 15 points apiece, and the Minnesota Timberwolves cruised to a 115-93 win over the host Orlando Magic on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Anthony Edwards and Jaden McDaniels scored 15 points apiece, and the Minnesota Timberwolves cruised to a 115-93 win over the host Orlando Magic on Friday night. Rudy Gobert added 14 points and nine rebounds for Minnesota, which won its second game in a row to start the season. Ayo Dosunmu finished with 14 points and nine assists, and LaMelo Ball chipped in 12 points. Wendell Carter Jr. tallied 20 points and nine rebounds to lead Orlando, which dropped its second straight game under first-year head coach Sean Sweeney. Franz Wagner recorded 18 points before fouling out, and Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs finished with 14 points apiece. Minnesota shot 42.9% (42 of 98) from the field and 37.8% (14 of 37) from 3-point range. Orlando shot 44% (37 of 84) overall but only 20.5% (8 of 39) from beyond the arc. The Timberwolves led 57-45 at the half. A fast start allowed Minnesota to seize a double-digit lead as early as the first quarter. Joan Beringer made a running dunk off a pass from Dosunmu to put the Timberwolves on top 24-13 with 1:05 remaining in the session. In the second quarter, the Timberwolves increased their lead to as many as 17 points. Ball dished a pass to Edwards, who finished with a layup to make it 57-40 with 56 seconds remaining before the break. Orlando scored the final five points of the first half on a 3-pointer by Suggs and a pair of free throws by Goga Bitadze. The Magic fell further behind in the third quarter. They gave up a 17-3 run to finish the quarter, which ended with the Timberwolves leading 86-60. Ball and Edwards combined for the first eight points of Minnesota's third-quarter run. Beringer added a free throw and a dunk, Dosunmu made a layup, and Trey Lyles contributed a 3-pointer and a pull-up jump shot. The Magic trailed by double digits throughout the fourth quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett fuel Raptors past Wizards
item.description: Scottie Barnes collected 28 points and 14 rebounds and RJ Barrett added 23 and nine, respectively, lifting the visiting Toronto Raptors to a 112-102 victory over the Washington Wizards on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Scottie Barnes collected 28 points and 14 rebounds and RJ Barrett added 23 and nine, respectively, lifting the visiting Toronto Raptors to a 112-102 victory over the Washington Wizards on Friday. Barnes made 12 of 26 shots from the floor to offset eight turnovers for the Raptors, who never trailed in the contest. Kawhi Leonard recorded 16 points and eight rebounds and Immanuel Quickley added 12 points and six assists for Toronto. The Raptors shot 44% from the floor and enjoyed a decisive 52-32 edge in points in the paint. Trae Young highlighted his 22-point, 12-assist performance by draining four 3-pointers, with his last pulling Washington within five points at 94-89 with 8:04 to play. Toronto responded with an 11-3 run, with Barrett making a pair of driving layups and an 18-foot jumper in that stretch. Washington countered by scoring five straight points before Leonard made a pair of baskets and Barnes converted a three-point play to effectively seal the win. Kyshawn George had 11 points on 2-of-9 shooting while committing eight of the Wizards' 23 turnovers. Washington's AJ Dybantsa, the top overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, sat out his second straight game with a sprained left ankle. Barnes' dunk extended Toronto's lead to 76-66 with 2:50 remaining in the third quarter before Young sank his third 3-pointer of the evening, igniting an 11-2 run. Justin Champagnie had a pair of layups and converted an alley-oop dunk during that sequence before Jamison Battle drilled a 3-pointer just before the end of the quarter for Toronto. The Raptors put the game on ice by outscoring the Wizards by a 31-25 margin in the fourth quarter. George sank a pair of free throws to cut Toronto's lead to 16-11 with 4:32 remaining in the first before the Raptors responded with an 18-10 run to end the quarter. Barnes drained two jumpers and a 3-pointer during the late surge. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hot-shooting Hawks set franchise mark with 47-point rout of Hornets
item.description: Jalen Johnson and reserve Aaron Wiggins each scored 19 points as visiting Atlanta blew out the Charlotte Hornets 128-81 on Friday, the biggest margin of victory in Hawks history.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jalen Johnson and reserve Aaron Wiggins each scored 19 points as visiting Atlanta blew out the Charlotte Hornets 128-81 on Friday, the biggest margin of victory in Hawks history. The 47-point gap topped the old record of 46 points set in a 126-80 victory over the visiting Sacramento Kings on Nov 15, 2017. Nickeil Alexander-Walker put up 14 points, CJ McCollum posted 13 points, Dyson Daniels contributed 11 points and nine rebounds and Corey Kispert also had 11 points for Atlanta, which won its second game in a row to start the season. Onyeka Okongwu added 10 points as the Hawks shot 50.5% from the field. Johnson supplied eight assists. It was a miserable home opener for the Hornets, who won two nights earlier at Brooklyn to start their campaign. They committed 27 turnovers. Naz Reid scored 17 points for Charlotte and Grayson Allen came off the bench for 11 points. Both players were in their home debuts with the Hornets. Reserve Tidjane Salaun also scored 11 points. The Hawks were efficient on offense throughout the game. The gap reached 97-62 by the end of the third quarter. The Hornets couldn't even get it cranked up when the margin was out of hand, needing about 6 1/2 minutes to reach a double-digit total in the fourth quarter. Wiggins, who shot 7-for-9 from the field, hit 3 of 5 from 3-point range. Charlotte's Brandon Miller finished 2-for-14 from the field, including 1-for-11 on 3-point tries. He scored six points. The Hornets didn't apply much pressure, not attempting a 10th free throw until deep into the fourth quarter. Atlanta built a 15-point first-quarter lead. It was 33-20 through the opening quarter, with the Hornets willing to fire away from the perimeter. Charlotte was 2-for-15 on first-quarter 3-point attempts. The Hawks poured it on in the second quarter to claim a 68-43 halftime lead on the strength of Wiggins' 15 points along with 13 points apiece from Johnson and McCollum. Atlanta benefited from Charlotte's 14 first-half turnovers. The Hornets played again without injured Kon Knueppel (hamstring), Coby White (calf) and Grant Williams (hamstring). --Field Level Media

item.title: Police officers resign after fatal shooting of Black child in Mississippi
item.description: A police officer in Mississippi who fatally shot a 1-year-old Black child in a Walmart parking lot in June and the interim police chief in the city where the shooting took place have resigned, local officials said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: A police officer in Mississippi who fatally shot a 1-year-old Black child in a Walmart parking lot in June and the interim police chief in the city where the shooting took place have resigned, local officials said on Friday. Hunter Foster, the officer who shot the child, resigned from the Senatobia Police Department, Mayor Greg Graves said on Friday, without specifying whether he was asked to resign or did so on his own. Angelica Maze, who was the interim chief for the department, also stepped down, according to a resignation letter reported by local media. Foster had fired his gun at a moving vehicle in response to a shoplifting call in Senatobia in June, killing 1-year-old Kohen Wiley. The fatal shooting of the child had sparked calls from civil rights advocates for accountability. The child's family has said the shooting was not justified, but Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch said this week that "the use of force was justified" and cleared the officer of criminal wrongdoing. Although Foster was cleared, his lawyer, Martin Zummach, told NBC News that his client "resigned for the good of the city and the police department and to permit the process of healing." Prominent civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who is representing the child's family, said they were calling for a Department of Justice investigation and that accountability cannot end at the resignation of the officer. The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation said after the shooting in mid-June that law enforcement officers responded to a shoplifting call at Walmart and encountered two adults and a juvenile child fleeing from the store into a vehicle. Officers attempted to stop the vehicle, but the driver drove in their direction, the bureau added, saying that an officer "then discharged their weapon and the vehicle fled the scene." Footage released from the incident showed Foster running out of the Walmart with other officers after an employee said suspected shoplifters were attempting to flee. While officials have alleged the child's mother and her friend stole diapers, the two women have not been charged. "No mother should have to bury her baby over an allegation of shoplifting diapers," Crump said on Friday. Former Senatobia Police Chief Harold Vanderford was fired in September after media outlets reported he used racist slurs against Black people in text messages.

item.title: Democrat on US FCC urges broadcast industry to be more aggressive confronting the agency
item.description: The sole Democratic member of the Federal Communications Commission on Friday urged the broadcast industry to take a more aggressive approach in confronting the Trump administration's actions toward major US networks and stations.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The sole Democratic member of the Federal Communications Commission on Friday urged the broadcast industry to take a more aggressive approach in confronting the Trump administration's actions toward major US networks and stations. FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez called on the National Association of Broadcasters to address the administration's efforts to challenge broadcasters on a series of fronts, including a warning from FCC Chair Brendan Carr that US broadcast networks could violate their regulatory obligations by airing "entirely fake polls" before the November 3 election . "This administration is running a coordinated, government-wide effort to reshape the media into its sanctioned messenger," Gomez warned, adding that Carr was seeking to pressure networks into not running polls the administration dislikes, which she said was not proper. Carr, who has repeatedly faced pressure from President Donald Trump to crack down on US broadcasters and journalists, in April ordered an unprecedented early license review for all eight of Disney's (DIS.N) company-owned ABC TV stations. A spokesperson for Carr did not immediately comment. NAB President Curtis LeGeyt said in a statement that the group appreciated Gomez's "recognition of the value of local broadcasters and her commitment to the First Amendment principles that underpin a free press." "We will continue working with her and all policymakers to protect broadcasters’ rights," he said. Gomez said the NAB had been "largely quiet through the first year of this censorship and control campaign" but that it had not stayed "completely silent." An "industry confronting a coordinated effort to turn licensing authority into leverage over election-year coverage needs more than a couple of tempered statements," she added. In April, the NAB said the Disney early-renewal decision "creates significant uncertainty for all broadcasters" and argued the "FCC must be careful to avoid actions that create further instability for the local stations viewers and listeners depend on." The FCC also said earlier this year that late-night and daytime talk shows are no longer bona fide news programs that are exempt from equal-time rules for interviews with political candidates.

item.title: Streaking Maple Leafs, Oilers collide as Mike Babcock faces old team
item.description: The visiting Toronto Maple Leafs will have their three-game win streak tested against the high-flying Edmonton Oilers on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The visiting Toronto Maple Leafs will have their three-game win streak tested against the high-flying Edmonton Oilers on Saturday night. The Maple Leafs edged the New York Rangers 5-4 in a back-and-forth game on Thursday. Defenseman Troy Stecher provided the unlikely game-winner with less than 30 seconds remaining in regulation for his first goal since February. "I really liked our game," head coach Jim Hiller said. "That was probably our best game of the year through 60 minutes for me. The Rangers played good, pushed us hard, but we didn't have those lulls and dips. In fact I thought we ended up pushing and got momentum back." Toronto's fourth line came to the rescue Thursday, combining for seven points as Brandon Duhaime and Teddy Blueger scored their first goals with the Maple Leafs. Hiller was delighted to see his depth players step up during alternate captain John Tavares' ongoing absence. "Everybody always loves it when those guys get rewarded with goals and points because they do the dirty work, blocking shots, getting forechecks going," Hiller said. "I think that's what makes the night extra special." If he starts again, Toronto will hope for a bounce-back performance from netminder Sergei Bobrovsky, who allowed four goals on 25 shots even as he moved into a sixth-place tie with Henrik Lundqvist in all-time wins for goaltenders. Bobrovsky, who signed a three-year, $21 million contract with the Maple Leafs in the offseason, has posted a .895 save percentage through eight games. The Oilers sit atop the Pacific Division after a 6-5 shootout win over the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes. Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl continued their early-season tears, combining for ten points to complete the comeback. "I thought this was the best opportunity for our team was to play them tonight," head coach Mike Babcock said of the heavyweight bout. "For me, it was like a gift. We've got a lot of lessons there today, and then I think you build off those lessons. And we have to learn to be way more resilient. When we bend, we can't break like that. You've just got to hang in there." The dynamic duo has combined for 68 points against the Maple Leafs in their careers and will have every reason to be optimistic against a short-handed Toronto blue line. Edmonton, though, will be without No. 1 goaltender Devon Levi, who was placed on injured reserve Friday. It was unclear what Levi injured or when, as he finished out the shootout win against Carolina. Tristan Jarry will make his fourth start of the season against the Maple Leafs, while Matt Tomkins was recalled from the Bakersfield Condors under emergency conditions to serve as backup. In addition to Chris Tanev (upper-body injury), Toronto will be without defenseman Nick Blankenburg, who left the game on Thursday after taking a heavy hit in the third period. Mattias Ekholm has been placed on injured reserve for the Oilers and Jason Dickinson remains sidelined. The game will mark Babcock's first time coaching against the Maple Leafs since his contentious 2019 departure, which preceded a nearly seven-year hiatus from the NHL. "Because they asked me," Babcock said of why he returned to the league. "So if they hadn't asked me, I'd have never done it. But when those kids asked me, they want to win and I think they should, so I'm gonna try to help." --Field Level Media

item.title: Typhoon Champi sweeps past Taiwan, one dead and 500 injured
item.description: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday killing one person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continues to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday killing one person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continues to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast. At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi is weakening though still packing gusts of around 126 kph (78 mph) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA). The storm was about 150 km (93 miles) east of Taiwan, the CWA said, having glanced the island's northeast coast in the early hours of Saturday. The storm's forecast track shows it is now turning north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan. Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remaining at one, a man swept away by waves from the island of Liuqiu, with 527 injuries during the heavy wind and torrential rain. Taipower said at one point more than 167,000 homes had lost electricity, though most had been reconnected. The transport ministry said 242 flights were cancelled, though that was an improvement from Friday when the number was almost 1,000. In the capital Taipei, there were downed trees and on-off squally rain showers. A swathe of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Saturday. Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too.

item.title: Marquez shrugs off crash to take pole at wet Australian Grand Prix
item.description: Ducati's Marc Marquez swept to a stunning pole position at the Australian MotoGP in a wet and slippery qualifying on Saturday, with championship leader and title rival Jorge Martin finishing fourth-quickest.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ducati's Marc Marquez swept to a stunning pole position at the Australian MotoGP in a wet and slippery qualifying on Saturday, with championship leader and title rival Jorge Martin finishing fourth-quickest. The conditions were treacherous at a soggy Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit, and Marquez crashed early in the second qualifying session as he lost his front and slid off onto the grass. The defending champion was unscathed, though, and sprinted through the Ducati garage, swapping bikes before laying down a scorching 1:34.203 to clinch his fourth pole of the season. "I just tried to cover my big mistake! You cannot crash in the first lap, because that means that you don't have a lap time," seven-times MotoGP champion Marquez said. "So it was a mistake on that turn four, but the team was ready with the other bike. I kept my focus, I tried to find the same feeling as I had in free practice. The last lap is the one that I did all in, and it was a good lap." Marquez's brother Alex of Gresini Racing took second, while LCR Honda's Johann Zarco completed the front row. Frenchman Zarco had come through the first qualifying session earlier on Saturday and capitalised on his knowledge of the shifting conditions. "It was stressful," Zarco said. "You think it's raining so you cannot switch to the medium, but then you go out and it is not raining anymore, and with the wind it's getting dry!" Aprilia's Martin will start from the second row in both Saturday's sprint and Sunday's race, giving Marquez a shot at overtaking him in the standings. With five rounds remaining in the season, including the Australian MotoGP, just two points separate the top two riders in the championship, with Martin on 355 and Marquez on 353. Martin's teammate Marco Bezzecchi, who was ninth-quickest in qualifying, is a somewhat distant third on 309. Earlier on Saturday, Australian rider Jack Miller of Pramac Racing topped the first qualifying session, much to the delight of home fans. Sunday's race will be MotoGP's last [USN:L6N46607H TEXT:"at Phillip Island,"] with the Australian Grand Prix moving to the streets of Adelaide next year.

item.title: Duke QB Walker Eget returns after apparent hand injury vs. Virginia
item.description: Duke quarterback Walker Eget returned to begin the second half of Friday night's game at Virginia after leaving on the team's first possession with an apparent hand injury at Charlottesville, Va.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Duke quarterback Walker Eget returned to begin the second half of Friday night's game at Virginia after leaving on the team's first possession with an apparent hand injury at Charlottesville, Va. The transfer from San Jose State missed the rest of the first half after the opening possession, which resulted in a Duke touchdown. Backup quarterback Dan Mahan played into the second quarter. Eget completed both of his first-quarter pass attempts for 43 yards before leaving. Eget entered the game completing 62.8% of his passes for 1,229 yards with eight touchdowns and two interceptions this season. Virginia led 13-7 at halftime. --Field Level Media

item.title: UK's Healey to give two state-backed lenders £20 billion capital boost in budget
item.description: Britain will provide £20.4 billion ($27.3 billion) of additional capital to the state's business lender and infrastructure bank in next week's budget, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing the Treasury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain will provide £20.4 billion ($27.3 billion) of additional capital to the state's business lender and infrastructure bank in next week's budget, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing the Treasury. The Treasury will allocate £15.4 billion ($20.6 billion) more to the National Wealth Fund and £5 billion ($7 billion) more to the British Business Bank over roughly half a decade, according to the report. "This additional capital will help more British businesses fulfil their potential, while getting investment behind the industries, infrastructure and places that create good jobs and drive lasting growth across the country," a Treasury spokesperson told the FT. The Treasury did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. The Treasury said the funding would help support around 100,000 jobs by 2035 in sectors including artificial intelligence, defence and green energy, the FT said. The measures are expected to be announced in finance minister John Healey's budget on Wednesday. ($1 = 0.7478 pounds)

item.title: Blakely wins world all-around title after injury setbacks
item.description: American Skye Blakely won the women's all-around title at the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships on Friday, completing a comeback from an Achilles injury that derailed her bid for the 2024 Paris Olympics.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: American Skye Blakely won the women's all-around title at the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships on Friday, completing a comeback from an Achilles injury that derailed her bid for the 2024 Paris Olympics. The 21-year-old scored 55.733 points across vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor exercise at Ahoy Arena to claim her first individual world title. Russia's Liudmila Roshchina took silver with 55.199, while China's Ke Qinqin, 16, finished third on 55.032. Blakely ruptured her right Achilles tendon during floor exercise training two days before the US Olympic trials in 2024, ending her bid to qualify for the Paris Games. She had also missed the Tokyo Olympic trials in 2021 after tearing an elbow ligament. The victory marks a breakthrough for Blakely, who previously won team gold at the 2022 and 2023 world championships but had not earned an individual world medal. She became the first American woman to win the world all-around title since Simone Biles in 2023.

item.title: US has for years asked Musk to alter Starlink service in Ukraine, Middle East, sources say
item.description: Well before the throttling this month of Ukraine's military access to Musk's satellite communications system, the Biden and Trump administrations had several times asked SpaceX to turn its Starlink service on or off in various countries, according to six former senior US officials.
item.dc:creator: Erin Banco, Joey Roulette
item.content:encoded: Well before the throttling this month of Ukraine's military access to Elon Musk's satellite communications system, the Biden and Trump administrations had several times asked SpaceX to turn its Starlink service on or off in various countries, according to six former senior US officials familiar with the matter. During the presidency of Joe Biden, the requests included switching off the service to prevent Iranian proxy militias in Yemen and Lebanon from using Starlink to communicate, and activating the service to provide internet access inside Iran and in Ukraine to support its military, said four of the former officials. Similarly, President Donald Trump's administration asked Musk, who is CEO of SpaceX, to make the service available in Iran following US-Israeli strikes in 2025 and 2026, in hopes it would bolster internet access and communications for anti-government protesters, a former senior Trump official and a person familiar with the matter told Reuters. All of the people spoke on condition of anonymity. The previous US requests about Starlink access are being reported here for the first time. The recent blowup over restrictions to Ukraine's use of SpaceX satellite services has raised questions about the ties between the US government and Musk, whose company owns systems vital to the US military and to US allies. The Biden-era and Trump requests to Musk show a close relationship in which US administrations rely to an unprecedented degree on a private-sector company to help implement foreign policy. The recent limits on Ukraine, despite being a US ally, have also rattled officials in Europe, some of whom argue that Europe must develop its own military satellite communications capabilities because no viable short-term alternative currently exists. STARSHIELD RESTRICTIONS HOBBLE UKRAINE MILITARY Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said last week that his country's access to Starshield, the military version of the Starlink system, had been intentionally limited, interfering with the performance of the country’s military drones. He also said the speeds were reduced for Starlink, which Ukraine uses for some military activities including defense against Russian missile attacks. Reuters has reported that [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"the order to throttle Starshield"] came from inside the White House. The Trump administration has acknowledged the slowdown but has not said whether it gave the order. The White House, contacted for comment, referred Reuters to Trump's remarks on Friday, when he said he had not spoken with Musk about Starlink access issues for Ukraine and that "if there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out." Halyna Yusypiuk, a spokesperson for the Ukrainian embassy in Washington, said Ukraine's priority is "to have the service restored to normal speed as soon as possible, as the lives of our people depend on it." SpaceX did not respond to requests for comment, although Musk said in a social media post earlier this week: “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately (by the president of the United States).” Democratic US Representative Jason Crow called on Friday for clarity about the recent changes to Ukraine's satellite service, saying there are risks to the US dependence on SpaceX. "Unelected billionaires and private corporations should not decide what is in the best interest of America's national security," Crow said. For Ukraine, the Starlink internet service has become the lifeblood of frontline communication between units, who say there is currently no rival to the capabilities of SpaceX's products. Starshield receivers, largely impervious to radio jamming, are used as onboard guidance systems and to provide links to a remote pilot for Ukrainian drones, including deep behind Russian lines inside Ukraine. MUSK'S INFLUENCE RAISES UNCERTAINTY Musk's role as the strong-willed CEO of a company with outsized influence over US national security has at times raised questions over who is making decisions about SpaceX's satellite services. The SpaceX CEO is "supposed to be a business executive, with government contracts, and he's essentially making huge foreign policy decisions," said Armand Musey, president of Summit Ridge Group, a satellite industry consultancy. "He's sufficiently ambiguous of a person that you don't know if his decisions are sort of his personal quirks, or it's because there's an influence elsewhere that's impacting him," Musey said. In previous years, Musk has moved to limit Ukraine’s access to Starlink. In 2022, according to Reuters reporting , Musk ordered SpaceX personnel to cut Starlink coverage in areas Ukraine was trying to retake, a move that surprised White House officials. Musk has said publicly that he refused a 2022 Ukrainian request to activate his satellite network in Crimea's port city of Sevastopol to aid an attack on Russia's fleet there, saying he feared complicity in a major act of war. The Biden administration at times relied on Musk to help implement policy, five of the former officials said. Biden officials coordinated with SpaceX to thwart US adversaries by cutting the service, and to help allies by expanding Starlink’s availability, they said. They added that discussions between the government and SpaceX, which usually included Pentagon and White House officials, often focused on preventing groups such as the Iranian-linked Houthis in Yemen and Hezbollah in Lebanon from using Starlink terminals. Biden officials several times shared intelligence with SpaceX that indicated that the Houthis and Hezbollah were using diverted Starlink terminals — hardware that made its way to the militants through intermediaries. In October 2023, during fighting between Israel and Hezbollah militants in southern Lebanon, intelligence officials told the White House that individuals linked to Hezbollah could have gained access to Starlink terminals. Officials had similar concerns about the Houthis in Yemen in 2024 during a US air campaign against the Iran-linked group, five of the officials said. In both cases, the administration contacted SpaceX and asked it to identify the terminals and shut them off. At least some of the terminals were deactivated, said two of the officials. In a 2024 submission to the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, SpaceX said it works closely with US government agencies to secure export authorizations where required and to safeguard technology in support of US national security objectives and foreign policy goals. Soon after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Biden officials pushed SpaceX to expand Starlink use for the Ukrainian military, said two of the former officials. In a separate instance, the Biden administration asked SpaceX to turn on Starlink in Iran during a protest movement launched in September 2022 after the death of Mahsa Amini, an Iranian arrested for not wearing her hijab properly, according to one of the former officials. Starlink terminals were moved into the country with the help of the administration, said the official, who declined to say how many were transferred. The Trump administration took a similar step earlier this year and discussed with Musk and SpaceX getting Starlink terminals into Iran and activated following US-Israeli strikes in the country in June 2025 and again in February 2026, a former senior Trump official and a person familiar with the matter told Reuters. Neither the Trump administration nor SpaceX has publicly confirmed that those terminals were turned on. The Wall Street Journal reported in February that the US government had sent thousands of Starlink terminals into Iran. Iran's delegation to the UN did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Tyrrell Hatton, Ian Poulter join LIV Golf exodus
item.description: LIV Golf lost two more big-name players, with Englishmen Tyrrell Hatton and Ian Poulter announcing Friday they will not sign on for LIV 2.0.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: LIV Golf lost two more big-name players, with Englishmen Tyrrell Hatton and Ian Poulter announcing Friday they will not sign on for LIV 2.0. Hatton, 35, posted a brief statement to Instagram announcing his decision. "Wanted to confirm that I will not be a part of LIV 2.0," he wrote. "A big thank you to everyone for continued support," he continued. "I am excited for what the next chapter of my career holds." Hatton joined LIV in 2024 and had one tournament win -- LIV Nashville that same year. He was part of captain Jon Rahm's Legion XIII, winner of the 2025 season championship. Poulter, 50, said he made his decision after discussing his playing future with his family and team. "Ultimately, the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests was something that I felt was right for me at this stage of my life and career," Poulter said in an Instagram post. Poulter was among the first players to sign with LIV Golf at its inception in 2022. He and countryman Lee Westwood have been two of the most outspoken supporters of the Saudi-backed league, which has been accused by many critics of dividing the professional golf world. Poulter and Westwood served as the co-captains of the all-English Majesticks GC that included Laurie Canter and Sam Horsfield for the 2026 season. Majesticks finished 12th in the 13-team league. Tom McKibbin added his name to the list later Friday when he announced his decision to play full-time on the DP World Tour going forward. The 23-year-old native of Northern Ireland, who counts Rory McIlroy as a countryman and mentor, won one DP World Tour event before joining Rahm and Legion XIII in 2025. "Joining LIV Golf was the right decision for me at the time, and I'm grateful for everything it has given me," McKibbin wrote on Instagram. "... I've taken time to think about what's best for me and I am confident (returning to the DP World Tour) is the right decision to help me achieve my goals." Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced earlier this year that it would end its financial support of LIV Golf. CEO Scott O'Neil has lined up funding for LIV 2.0 as the league goes through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings, with plans to play a 10-event schedule in 2027 that includes five events in the United States and five internationally. However, Hatton, Poulter and McKibbin join a growing list of players who will not return that includes Rahm, Sergio Garcia and David Puig of Spain, as well as Abraham Ancer, Charles Howell III, Adrian Meronk, Louis Oosthuizen and Thomas Pieters. Other marquee names, including Bryson DeChambeau, Cam Smith and Joaquin Niemann, have not declared yet what they intend to do by Sunday's registration deadline. "Clearly, LIV Golf has divided opinion," Poulter wrote. "But to be part of the founding group that took world class golf around the globe, showcased our great game to a new audience, built a team brand in Majesticks GC, helped innovate tournament formats and establish a leading community impact program in Little Sticks, is something I will be forever proud of. And that's just scratching the surface of what we achieved together. "Change is never easy and it's fair to say professional golf has experienced plenty of it over the last few years. But I've always believed that change can create opportunity and ultimately lead to positive outcomes. There will undoubtedly be more changes ahead, but I am confident the game will continue to grow, evolve, and deliver the very best for golf fans around the world." Poulter will likely need to serve a one-year suspension from the date of his most recent LIV event before being eligible to play on the Champions Tour, similar to former LIV player Henrik Stenson, who made his Champions debut earlier this year. The DP World Tour has also announced it will not grant membership to LIV Golf players in 2027, which Poulter needs in order to be eligible to be a Ryder Cup captain or vice captain for Europe in the future. Meanwhile, Poulter's eldest son, Luke, 22, plays golf for the University of Florida and has competed in the Walker Cup. Joshua Poulter, 14, is his youngest son. Ian and his wife, Katie, also have two daughters. He said he plans to devote more time to helping Luke and Joshua in their golf pursuits and also growing his YouTube channel. "I'm genuinely excited about this next chapter. I'm looking forward to spending more time with my family, continuing to develop The Postman YouTube channel, sharing more of my life, golf, experiences and competing in some senior events," Poulter wrote. "Something I am also particularly looking forward to is being able to spend more time helping Luke as he pursues his career in professional golf, and Joshua as he looks to develop as a golfer in his teenage years. Having spent so many years travelling the world chasing my own golfing dreams, the opportunity to now spend more time supporting my boys as they chase theirs is something that means a great deal to me. "After all these years, golf has given me so much, and I'm excited about what lies ahead, both on and off the course. Thanks again to everyone who has been part of the journey so far! We certainly aren't done yet!" --Field Level Media

item.title: Legendary Rams RB Lawrence McCutcheon dies at 76
item.description: Legendary Los Angeles Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon died Friday after a battle with Parkinson's disease. He was 76.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Legendary Los Angeles Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon died Friday after a battle with Parkinson's disease. He was 76. McCutcheon was a Pro Bowl selection in five straight seasons (1973-77) for the Rams and still ranks fourth all-time on the club's rushing list with 6,186 yards over eight seasons from 1972-79. McCutcheon was the franchise's leading rusher when his Los Angeles career ended. He now ranks behind Marshall Faulk (6,959), Eric Dickerson (7,245) and Steven Jackson (10,138) on the club's list. "It is with great sadness that we share the passing of our husband, brother, father, grandfather, and great grandfather, Lawrence McCutcheon," McCutcheon's family said in a statement. "Clutch passed away on October 23 with family at his bedside following a long, courageous battle with Parkinson's disease. "Through a decade-long playing career and another 32 years in the Rams' front office, Clutch earned the respect and admiration of teammates, opposing players, colleagues, and fans alike. Clutch will be missed and remembered forever. We are thankful to those in our community who have reached out with love and support." McCutcheon finished his playing career with the Denver Broncos (1980), Seattle Seahawks (1980) and Buffalo Bills (1981). Overall, he rushed for 6,578 yards and 26 touchdowns and caught 198 passes for 1,799 yards and 13 scores in 109 career games (82 starts). McCutcheon participated in 11 playoff games for the Rams and famously threw a 24-yard touchdown pass to Ron Smith in the third quarter of Super Bowl XIV. That gave Los Angeles a 19-17 lead before it eventually lost 31-19 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Jan. 20, 1980. McCutcheon was a third-round pick in 1972 out of Colorado State, also known as the Rams. He played at Colorado State from 1969-71 and still ranks seventh all-time in rushing yards (2,917). McCutcheon was inducted into the Colorado State Athletics Hall of Fame in 1989. After his playing career, McCutcheon returned to the Rams as a scout in 1982 and served in many roles -- including director of player personnel for seven years -- before retiring in 2016. "The Los Angeles Rams are deeply saddened by the passing of Lawrence McCutcheon," the team said in a statement. "His impact on this organization spanned generations, and he embodied what it means to be a Ram. A five-time Pro Bowl running back and once the franchise's all-time leading rusher, he later served in our front office as a scout and director of player personnel. His legacy is woven into the fabric of our team. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the McCutcheon family as we celebrate a life that gave so much to the Rams and to our game." Cornerback Daylon McCutcheon, the son of Lawrence, was a member of the Cleveland Browns from 1999-2006. McCutcheon's family asked that, in lieu of flowers, those wishing to honor him please donate to the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research. --Field Level Media

item.title: Líder da Coreia do Norte pede “revolução militar” ao exigir unidades militares mais fortes
item.description: O líder norte-coreano Kim Jong Un pediu que as companhias do Exército do país fossem transformadas em unidades de combate de elite e autossuficientes durante uma reunião de dois dias de comandantes de companhia em Pyongyang, informou a agência de notícias estatal KCNA no sábado (horário local).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O líder norte-coreano Kim Jong Un pediu que as companhias do Exército do país fossem transformadas em unidades de combate de elite e autossuficientes durante uma reunião de dois dias de comandantes de companhia em Pyongyang, informou a agência de notícias estatal KCNA no sábado (horário local). O evento ressaltou a prioridade política consistente de Kim de fortalecer as Forças Armadas. Em um discurso proferido na conferência de comandantes de companhias do Exército da Coreia do Norte, realizada nos dias 22 e 23 de outubro — que, segundo a KCNA, foi o primeiro encontro de todo o Exército desde o 9º Congresso do partido governista da Coreia do Norte, em fevereiro —, Kim pediu que todas as companhias se preparassem plenamente para que “a meta do fortalecimento militar da nova era” pudesse ser alcançada. “Vamos tornar o Exército mais forte e acelerar uma revolução militar ao nosso estilo”, disse Kim. Durante o 9º Congresso do partido governista da Coreia do Norte, em fevereiro — que define os rumos do país para os próximos cinco anos —, Kim pediu o fortalecimento das Forças Armadas convencionais, além de reafirmar os esforços para desenvolver armas nucleares e mísseis.

item.title: Boeing supplier dispute has halted 777 freighter production for two months, sources say
item.description: Boeing's dispute with a small Florida-based supplier has halted production of its 777 freighter for nearly two months and disrupted output of the 767, including freighters and KC-46 aerial refueling tankers, according to Boeing workers and court filings.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole
item.content:encoded: Boeing's (BA.N) dispute with a small Florida-based supplier has halted production of its 777 freighter for nearly two months and disrupted output of the 767, including freighters and KC-46 aerial refueling tankers, according to Boeing workers and court filings. Boeing filed a complaint in August alleging supplier Vaero had stopped delivering a critical wing component known as the trailing-edge rib kit, stalling work at the Everett, Washington, wing-production facility that supports the 777 freighter and 767 programs, according to a copy of the complaint reviewed by Reuters. The disruption was costing Boeing as much as $6.5 million a day, the complaint said. Boeing said in the complaint that the trailing-edge rib kit was an "indispensable" part and Vaero was the sole supplier. Although the companies reached a settlement in late September, production of the 777 freighter has yet to resume, according to three Boeing workers familiar with the matter. They declined to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. The dispute also disrupted production of the 767, a widebody cargo and military aircraft, the people said. Since the settlement, Boeing has received some parts for the 767 line, according to one of the workers. The prolonged disruption highlights the fragility of aerospace supply chains, showing how a dispute involving a single supplier can halt production of aircraft that remain in strong demand. The lawsuit was first reported by Law.com in August, but the nearly two-month production disruption has not previously been reported. Boeing declined to comment. Vaero did not respond to requests for comment. BRINGING PRODUCTION IN-HOUSE Boeing is trying to bring production of the trailing-edge rib kit in-house, according to two of the people. The component is used in wing assembly for the 767 and current-generation 777 freighter. Boeing's 777X, which uses composite wings, has not been affected. Without the Vaero parts, Boeing removed two partially assembled 777 freighters from its final assembly line, according to one Boeing worker. Using data from aviation consultancy IBA, Reuters identified one of the aircraft as destined for FedEx (FDX.N) . FedEx did not respond to a request for comment. Boeing has delivered 21 777 freighters so far this year, company data show. It also has a handful of freighters whose wings were assembled before the dispute and could still be delivered before year-end, according to two of the Boeing workers.

item.title: Amazon cloud capacity sold out through 2027, CEO Jassy says
item.description: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on Friday that Amazon Web Services' cloud computing capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with significant commitments extending into 2028, on growing demand for AI infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Amazon (AMZN.O) CEO Andy Jassy said on Friday that Amazon Web Services' cloud computing capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with significant commitments extending into 2028, on growing demand for AI infrastructure. In a video podcast with Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Ben Horowitz and general partner Erik Torenberg, Jassy said Amazon is struggling to keep pace with the insatiable demand from AI labs and enterprises. Earlier this year, Amazon had said it would spend [USN:L4N43X10O TEXT:"about $220 billion"] in capital expenditure for 2026 Jassy said the company "could invest a lot more and it wouldn't be a bad use of capital," considering cloud-computing capacity for 2026 is already sold out "2027 is largely sold out. We always leave a certain amount for on demand and our inference service bedrock, or EC2, but largely sold out all the big chunks. A good chunk of 2028 is sold out," he said EC2 is an AWS service that provides cloud servers for running applications, while Bedrock gives customers access to AI models to build generative AI applications Amazon is scheduled to report third quarter results on October 29

item.title: Bulls storm back from early deficit to beat Bucks
item.description: Norman Powell scored 25 points and rookie Caleb Wilson added 21 on Friday to help the visiting Chicago Bulls earn a 132-125 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Norman Powell scored 25 points and rookie Caleb Wilson added 21 on Friday to help the visiting Chicago Bulls earn a 132-125 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks. Leonard Miller had 19 points, while Jalen Smith chipped in 14 points and 13 rebounds for Chicago, which rebounded after suffering a 43-point loss to the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday. Buddy Hield scored 13, Isaac Okoro had 12 and Tre Jones tallied 11 points and eight assists for the Bulls, who trailed by 15 points after the first quarter. Tyler Herro led Milwaukee with 34 points, followed by Jaime Jaquez Jr.'s 19 points and 11 boards. Kyle Kuzma scored 14 and Myles Turner had 12, while Ryan Rollins, AJ Green and Kel'el Ware scored 11 apiece for the Bucks, who lost their second straight to open the season. Rookie Brayden Burries made a 3-pointer and Ware scored around the rim to give the Bucks a five-point lead with 2:55 left in the third quarter. Smith beat the third-quarter buzzer with a dunk that cut the Bulls' deficit to 104-102 entering the fourth. Chicago scored the first six points of the final quarter and grabbed a 108-104 lead on Wilson's slam. The Bulls pushed the lead to eight on Hield's trey with 7:19 remaining. With Milwaukee trailing by five, Herro connected on back-to-back 3-pointers, returning the lead to the Bucks. Wilson made two free throws to put the Bulls ahead 124-123 with 1:16 left. After Jones picked off Rollins' pass, Wilson made another pair from the foul line to push the lead to three. A missed 3-pointer by Herro and two more free throws from Powell gave the Bulls a five-point cushion with 20 seconds left. Wilson's steal and Jones' subsequent two foul shots sealed Chicago's victory. Milwaukee jumped out to a 19-6 lead on Herro's first triple less than five minutes in. Green sank a 3-pointer in the closing seconds of the first quarter to give the Bucks a 32-17 advantage.
